_comment: Bash scope policy per handbook ADR 0004 Track 2. Loaded by hooks/pre-tool-use.sh on every Bash tool call. deny_patterns are universal (no agent can bypass). universal_allow lists POSIX shell builtins + harmless flow-control that pass FIRST_TOKEN check for any role. tiers are named shared binary sets; agent_allow entries starting with '@' are resolved to the matching tier at lookup time by pre-tool-use.sh. agent_allow is per-role positive scope; agents not in agent_allow have no Bash by default. Add to agent_allow or tiers only via tool-matrix-change decision (cto proposes at company scope / pca proposes at project scope, cso reviews, CEO approves, eng-platform installs at company scope / project's eng-lead installs at project scope) per SYSTEM_INVARIANTS.md §6 + ADR 0014 §4 single-writer-per-scope.
_compound_command_note: BUG-098 (v1.17.3): every simple command of a Bash line is checked against the per-role allow-list, not only the first: segments after ; && || | newline, inside $( ) ` ` <( ) and double quotes, behind env/xargs/nice/timeout/nohup, and inside bash -c / eval / find -exec (hooks/lib/bash-segments.sh). Heredoc bodies, comments and quoted arguments are data. A line that cannot be parsed reliably is denied (deny:parse:). The universal deny-list still applies regex-wide.
_v08_rename_note: Per ADR 0014 §1, agent_allow keys renamed at v0.8.0: ca→cto (company scope), project cto→pca (project scope), coo→eng-lead, cdo→design-lead, cpo→product-lead. Project-vpe removed (absorbed by eng-lead per §2); vpe key now refers to the optional company-scope VPE gated by feature_toggles.vpe_enabled. eng-platform allow-list extended with npm/npx/node for npm:publish capability per ADR 0014 §3.
_sql_deny_patterns_comment: BUG-066 / decisions#272: DDL-destructive patterns for SQL payloads. Applied ONLY when FIRST_TOKEN is turso and the invocation is db shell/exec. Patterns are anchored (^) so prose inside SQL string literals (INSERT INTO … VALUES ('DROP TABLE foo')) does not trigger them — only a statement that BEGINS with the destructive keyword fires. For non-turso SQL executors (psql, sqlite3), deny_patterns still apply full-string and catch DROP TABLE anywhere in the command.
_sql_protected_comment: decisions#303 R5a / #308 (security_audit_log#155, #161, #163): audit-immutability rules the pre-tool-use SQL gate applies to EVERY statement any DB CLI receives (argument, redirect file, here-string, heredoc), case-insensitively, after SQL comments are removed and prose literals emptied — never on prose. no_delete: DELETE, REPLACE / INSERT OR REPLACE and ALTER TABLE … RENAME|DROP are denied on these tables. frozen_columns: an UPDATE whose SET clause assigns one of these columns is denied ('*' = every column); corrections are recorded as audit_events rows. set_once: the column may only be set by an UPDATE whose WHERE carries '<col> IS NULL' (the documented approval UPDATE). db_clock_tables: an INSERT naming created_at is denied — the DB clock sets it. The schema triggers (scripts/schema.sql, R5b) are the backstop for routes this Bash gate can't see.
_single_writer_gh_comment: FEAT-052 — single-writer §4 gate for GitHub writes via the gh CLI. With the deprecated github MCP removed, gh is the GitHub mechanism and gh is broadly allow-listed, so WRITE operations must be restricted to the single writer per scope (eng-lead at project scope, eng-platform at company scope) — exactly like git push/commit/merge in Track 2d. pre-tool-use.sh Track 2d matches the Bash command against these patterns; a match by any non-eng-lead/eng-platform subagent is denied (main operator thread is exempt, same as the git gate). Read-only gh (view/list/diff/checks/status, api GET, repo clone/view, release download) is NOT listed and stays open to all gh-allowed agents. gh api with field flags (-f/-F/--field/--raw-field) defaults to POST, so it is gated unless an explicit -X GET is present — that special case is handled in pre-tool-use.sh, not here. Verb-explicit (ERE has no negative lookahead); additions are cheap.
_agent_role_deny_comment: R3 defense-in-depth (security incident class: framework-bug-enabled agent cloud-writes). These patterns deny cloud-mutating CLI commands for any agent role (cos, cfo, …, eng-platform, pca, eng-lead, …). The CEO/operator path (ROLE in {unknown, ceo, operator}, i.e. main thread without a subagent dispatch) is exempt — the human at the keyboard is exercising direct authority. Read-only invocations are NOT blocked: 'az ... show|list|account|version|help', 'terraform fmt|validate|plan|init|workspace|providers|version' continue to pass. Cloud mutations MUST only ever happen via the CEO-triggered terraform-apply GitHub workflow (deployment-spec / eng-platform-spec gated by Track 4), never via local CLI from an agent. Patterns are deliberately verb-explicit (vs negative lookahead, which ERE does not support); the universe of mutating verbs is open-ended but the high-risk ones are well-known and additions are cheap.
_cloud_cli_read_only_comment: BUG-076. R3 for agent roles: these CLIs run read-only. hooks/lib/cloud-cli.sh checks the parsed argv of every command against this list and denies everything else, including an unlisted leading flag. agent_role_deny_patterns above is only the fallback for lines argv can't see into (code readers, unparsable lines). shape: first = first word of the path; last = last word of the path; second = second word (service operation); any = a read verb present and no write word, for CLIs whose verb can be followed by positional names.
_exec_scope_comment: BUG-103, ADR 0038. Roles with none of these binaries on their allow-list get hooks/lib/exec-scope.sh: bash/sh run only framework scripts, and allowed tools can't be used to run other commands. A role with an interpreter can run anything, so the check doesn't apply. Giving a role one of these binaries takes it out of the check: treat that as part of the tool-matrix-change.
_local_db_cli_comment: BUG-103: with db.provider=local (company or any project) the DB CLI is sqlite3, not turso. A role with turso gets sqlite3 there, same rights: both go through the same SQL gates, which also deny dot-commands such as .shell.
_gated_action_classes_comment: FEAT-040 Layer 3 — spec-lookup gate. Pre-tool-use.sh Track 4 matches the current Bash command against patterns here and requires an approved decision of the listed category in Turso (created within 7 days) before allowing. Bypass: main operator thread (agent_type absent from hook event = CEO direct session) — allowed but logged as [CEO-BYPASS] in input_summary for morning-brief retroactive spec tracking.
